R14.note: Searched all agent files for recovery, replay, retry, checkpoint, resume, persistence, queues, storage readers, timers and idempotency; traced src/server.ts, both routes, agent/loop.ts, tools/executor.ts, tools/registry.ts, tools/approvals.ts, all integrations, workflows/eligibility-check.ts, workers/reminders.ts, audit/recorder.ts, agent/budget.ts, control/kill-switch.ts, configuration, release manifest, deployment, Dockerfile, package scripts, tests and Terraform. No checkpoint or audit reader restores execution, and no automatic recovery/replay dispatcher exists. Runs build fresh in-memory messages and terminate with handoff on run errors; audit is an outbound Firehose writer. DynamoDB holds approval authorization, quota counters and halt flags, not recovery checkpoints; Terraform point-in-time recovery is a database backup setting with no application restore/replay consumer. Approval continuation requires a new input and authorizes an action previously withheld. The reminder worker reads current appointments and sends once per iteration; its CronJob disables failure retries and pod restarts. EHR, SMS, payments and the eligibility peer issue individual calls without a recovery resend loop; the eligibility workflow's refund is a direct action, not replay. Payment idempotency headers alone do not establish replay. Anthropic maxRetries concerns model requests, not re-execution of tool side effects. Tool errors are returned to the model, which could propose another action, but there is no implemented automatic resend or recovery from those results. Within the supplied repository, neither logs/checkpoints driving recovery nor automatic action replay was found, so the exact N/A condition holds.
